results.quote: In the worst case, OPT=Ω(log(n)), where OPT is the optimal solution value of Minimax-AlmostStable-sri and n is the number of agents, even when all preference lists are complete.
In the worst case, OPT=Θ(n), where OPT is the optimal solution value of Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-smi and n is the number of agents.
k-Max-AlmostStable-sri is NP-complete, even if k=1 and all preference lists are of length at most 10.

results.bound: \text{NP-complete for } k=1 \text{ and complete preference lists}
results.quote: k-Max-AlmostStable-sri is NP-complete, even if k=1 and all preference lists are complete.

The problem Minimax-AlmostStable-sri is para-NP-hard with respect to parameter κ=min_{M∈M}max_{a_i∈A}|bp_{a_i}(M)|, regardless of whether preference lists are of bounded length at most 10 or whether preferences are complete.
k-Max-AlmostStable-Perfect-smi is NP-complete, even if k=1 and all preference lists are of length at most 3.

The problem Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-smi is para-NP-hard with respect to parameter κ=min_{M∈M^+}max_{a_i∈A}|bp_{a_i}(M)| even if all preference lists are of length at most 3. By generalisation, this also applies to Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-sri.
k-Max-AlmostStable-sri is NP-complete for any fixed positive integer k.
k-Max-AlmostStable-Max-smi is NP-complete for any fixed positive integer k.
For any ε∈(0,1), the problem k-Max-AlmostStable-Max-smi is NP-complete for k=⌊N^{1-ε}⌋, where N is the number of agents.

Let I be an sri instance with n agents. If all preference lists of I are of length at most 2, then min_{M∈M}max_{a_i∈A}|bp_{a_i}(M)|≤1 and Algorithm 1 computes an optimal solution to Minimax-AlmostStable-sri in O(n) time.

Let I be an smi instance with n agents. If all preference lists of I are of length at most 2, then min_{M∈M^+}max_{a_i∈A}|bp_{a_i}(M)|≤1 and Algorithm 2 computes an optimal solution to Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-smi in O(n) time.

results.bound: \text{no approximation better than } 2 \text{ unless } P = NP
results.quote: The problems Minimax-AlmostStable-sri and Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-smi admit no polynomial-time approximation algorithms with a guarantee better than 2, unless P=NP.

Algorithm 3 returns a matching M of I such that |bp_i(M)|≤⌈d_i/2⌉ and thus max_{a_i∈A}|bp_i(M)|≤⌈d_max/2⌉. Furthermore, the algorithm returns a ⌈d_max/2⌉-approximation for Minimax-AlmostStable-sri and terminates in at most O(n·d_max^2) time.

results.bound: \text{not approximable within } N^{1/2} \text{ unless } P = NP
results.quote: Minimax-AlmostStable-Max-smi is not approximable within N^{1/2}, where N is the number of agents, unless P=NP.
